I was bullied in school for spending so much time on the computer. I was picked on, called a nerd. I failed a class or two after using our allotted computer time to learn HTML, CSS, and PHP so that I could design websites. I even had to talk to a fucking private investigator that the school hired after I showed other students what proxies were.

I'm not ashamed of this stuff. In fact, I'm proud of it. Until discovering the internet, I didn't feel like "part of a culture". I was an outcast. Afterwards, I was able to help shape one.

The people I conversed with online, in the primitive forums and chatrooms of the era, had similar stories. We were like Melvin from Sailor Moon. We didn't understand the real world, but there was something here that made us feel at home. Our minds were on the same wavelength. Of course, we argued, and had our disagreementsâ€”as I'm sure most cultures doâ€”but our core principles were carbon copies.

We were logical, creative, and wanted to learn. We believed in free speech, and the free exchange of information.

You have to understand that these things went unspoken. It's hard to explain. I mean, it's not like we formed an alliance and drew up a constitution on the topic. We didn't have to. I'm not sure what happened between then and now, but I'm starting to feel alone again.

Macklemore once rapped, "their culture was never ours to make better", referring to white performers taking over "black culture". You hear similar sentiments on Tumblr and reddit.

You also hear serious discussions on ending free speech and the free exchange of information we believed in.

But what about the "internet culture" that built the platforms upon which these non-geek, anti-freedom settlers are able to push for censorship.

You came here, settlers. You invaded our space without asking for permission, and now our code, our tools are being used against us. You're not a creator. Not an innovator. Not a geek.

However, despite this, I still disagree with Macklemore. I think the internet is one of the greatest achievements of mankind, and we should welcome with open arms those who want to join our culture, and make it better. But please stop making it worse.
